h1: Temporary Shortage List ends on 31 December 2026: what employers need to do
intro: Under the current Immigration Rules, the Temporary Shortage List stops applying to Certificates of Sponsorship assigned on or after 31 December 2026. If you’re planning to sponsor someone in a shortage role below degree level, you have weeks, not months, to act. Here’s what’s changing and what to do now.

sections.heading: What is the Temporary Shortage List?
sections.text:
Since 22 July 2025, most new Skilled Worker jobs must be skilled to degree level (RQF 6). The [Temporary Shortage List](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-temporary-shortage-list) is the exception. It lets employers sponsor workers in certain jobs at RQF levels 3 to 5, such as some engineering, construction and technical roles, while longer-term solutions are developed.

It was always meant to be temporary, and the Rules say it only applies to Certificates of Sponsorship assigned before 31 December 2026.

sections.heading: What happens after 31 December 2026
sections.text:
Unless the government changes the Rules, a Certificate of Sponsorship assigned on or after 31 December 2026 for a Temporary Shortage List job won’t qualify. The date that matters is when the certificate is assigned, not when the visa is decided.

A certificate can be used for up to three months after it’s assigned. So a certificate assigned in December 2026 still gives the worker time to apply in early 2027.

sections.heading: Could the Temporary Shortage List be extended?
sections.text:
Possibly. In July 2026 the Migration Advisory Committee recommended keeping shortage list access for 28 occupations for a further 18 months. That is advice to the government, not a change in the law, and no rule change had been published at the time of writing. The Home Office has said new Immigration Rules will start to be laid from December 2026, so it’s worth watching closely.

We’ll update our [news page](/news/) as soon as there’s an announcement.

sections.heading: What employers should do now
sections.text:
- Check whether the role is on the list using our [SOC code checker](/soc-code-checker/).
- If you plan to recruit, assign the Certificate of Sponsorship before 31 December 2026.
- Make sure the salary meets the rules for the job, including the going rate.
- Check you have enough certificates allocated on your licence, as requests take time.
- Tell the worker that new shortage list workers generally can’t bring a partner or children.

sections.heading: What about workers already in the UK?
sections.text: Workers who were already sponsored in jobs below degree level before 22 July 2025 can usually still extend their visa or change employer under transitional rules. The end of the Temporary Shortage List doesn’t remove that protection, but each case depends on the worker’s history, so check before assigning a new certificate.

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We help employers with [sponsor licences](/sponsor-licence/), certificate allocations and Skilled Worker applications. If you need to recruit before the deadline, contact us and we’ll check the role and salary first.

faqs.q: When does the Temporary Shortage List end?
faqs.a: Under the current Rules, it only applies to Certificates of Sponsorship assigned before 31 December 2026.

faqs.q: Does the worker have to apply before 31 December?
faqs.a: No. The certificate must be assigned before that date. The worker then has up to three months to use it.

faqs.q: Will the Temporary Shortage List be extended?
faqs.a: The Migration Advisory Committee recommended extending access for 28 occupations, but the government hasn’t confirmed a change.

faqs.q: Can shortage list workers bring their family?
faqs.a: New workers sponsored through the Temporary Shortage List generally can’t bring dependants.

faqs.q: What if the job isn’t on the Temporary Shortage List?
faqs.a: Jobs below degree level that aren’t on the list can’t usually be sponsored for new Skilled Worker applicants. Check the role in our SOC code checker or ask us about other options.
